newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Woodside confirms NW Shelf gas upgrade.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Woodside confirms NW Shelf gas upgrade.

text.p: Woodside Petroleum Ltd, operator of the North-West Shelf gas project, confirmed on Monday it planned to announce an upgrade of gas reserves at the project to about 24 trillion cubic feet (tcf) from about 15 tcf.

Asked to confirm a newspaper report that the company would announce the 60 percent increase in reserves, a spokesman said: "The gas figure looks correct, but condensate might be a little low." The Australian Financial Review reported earlier that Woodside would announce the gas upgrade as well as an upgrade for condensate reserves to about 500 million barrels.
The company said the announcement would be made on Monday.
The upgrades would be sufficient to lock in vital long term contracts for liquified natural gas with Japanese utilities, which buy the gas.
The partners in the project planned to boost LNG capacity to about 14.5 million tonnes from 7.5 million.
Woodside is operator of the project, off the north west coast of Western Australia.

Other equal partners are units of The Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd, The British Petroleum Co Plc, Japan Australia LNG (MiMi) Pty Ltd, a partnership of Mitsui & Co Ltd and Mitsubishi Corp, Chevron Corp and Royal Dutch/Shell Group.
At 0245 GMT (1.45 p.m.), Woodside shares were trading 11 cents up at A$9.23
